title: Alpha Trader
content: The idea is to know something before everyone else does then get out once everyone. Knows it, but I don't want to miss the last push higher as every Index Fund in the world comes in to Hoover jdsu. It's 3:58 p.m. the stock rallies to 13650. I tap a few buttons and I'm out, no way. Am I holding on until exactly 4 pm? It's way too dangerous. Sometimes with these index ads, too many people are positioned in advance and the buying from indexers is a big enough to offset all the day Traders, trying to take profit and the price crashes. Right? At 4:00, I'm satisfied with the profits of 37,750 minus brokerage brokerage is Tiny. So that's pretty much 3750 in my pocket Traders here. Keep 100% of p&l after brokerage fees. I settle into my seat to watch the last 2 minutes of fireworks. I feel like I should have a bucket of popcorn in my lap for this. It's 3:58 and 42 seconds. Tension builds in the room. There's always a ton of activity at the clothes even when there's no index at. So with the GDs, you thing happening, everyone. Is still here and everyone is locked and loaded for any last second opportunities. The greediest jdsu holders, hope for 1 last push higher. In the PDF, I show a picture of our trading screen. It's a sample showing Cisco Systems, not the jdsu window, but you'll get the idea. It's called the NASDAQ level 2 screen and it shows all the buyers on the left and sellers on the right. Our setup trades, mostly with Island B, trade and ARCA, we trade, using hot buttons assigned to the function keys, you set up, your default number of shares, some mindset to a 10000 and the F keys on the left are F1 cell and Island F2, sell on B trade, F3, cell and ARCA. Then to buy, you press F6 F7 and f8. You can operate these Keys very quickly because there's no confirmed. Dialogue, you press F1, you've instantly sold 1,000 shares of whatever stock window you're on, at the best bid available on Island. It's 3:58 and 50 seconds. I'm relaxed watching the prices. Been higher and lower in the jdsu window. My PC can barely keep up with the number of quotes and trades being jammed down the pipe but somehow it manages and the information continues to flow smoothly and impossibly fast. Then I noticed something weird. Jdsu is 141 bid on island and 1 140 ask on ARCA. Impossible. And it's not just there for a microc, it's just sitting there guys, you see this everyone's in the zone doing their own thing. Nobody's noticed the discrepancy I tap F1 and then f8 in succession selling 1,000 shares at 141, buying them back at 140 in less than a second. My p&l clicks, $1,000, higher. I do it 5 more times in about 5 Seconds. Still believing. This is probably too good to be true. I check my piano. This must be a mine fart, right wrong. My p&l is 5,000 higher than it was before I made the keystrokes dude. Arbitrage Gosh, I yell out to know 1 in particular, channeling. The 1994 Beastie Boys song Sabotage. Then I go nuts on the keyboard. F1 f8, F1 f8 F1 f8 F18 as fast as I can F1 f8, F1 f8, like a kid playing the 1980s coin up video game track and field. I paused for breath. At, check my p&l up another 12,000, and 12 seconds, the island, and ARA feeds both reset at 4:00 because the market makers drop out at the official close. I can do this Arbitrage, till 4 p.m. it's 3:59 and 35 seconds 24 more times. I press the F1 to f8 combo, my pnl jumps, another 24,000 in less than 30 seconds. My final p&l that day is 48,500 the best day. Anyone had ever realized in that office to that point, everyone gathers around my desk, my heart is pounding Vision. Pulsating, my body points to my p&l. Nice. Ever before, or after that day, did I ever see a market inverted like that again, it was a 1-time deal jdsu, stock never again traded higher than the 4 pm print on that day, July 26th 2000. It went on to lose 99% of its value in the next few years and just for fun. There's a chart in the PDF. That day was also high water for my p&l and the peak equity for my trading account. The NASDAQ made its final last gasp High, a few weeks later. Never in my life was on more overconfident than in the weeks immediately following that day. By mid 2002. I shut down my account with the balance below 35,000, and I was out looking for a real job by early, 2003 insult to injury. I had to accept a ridiculous, lowball bid to sell my M3 to pay my rent. I got crushed by a Confluence of overconfidence and some epic Market altering events. The 2, biggest changes that killed the day. Trading Community, were decimalisation, effective, April. 1 and the collapse in price of every single NASDAQ stock. My main strategy was to capture the bid offer on high price. Stocks each morning starting at 1999. I printed off, sheets listing, every NASDAQ stock, trading above a hundred dollars in 1999. That list was 4 pages long by 2002 it was 4 stocks. 4 Lessons Learned. 1 markets. Don't stay inefficient forever. The NASDAQ was wildly inefficient from 1998 to 2002. If you find an inefficiency make as much hay as you can, while the sun is shining, then stash away as many nuts as you can for winter. Winter.
